Context:
- CoreSight turns photos of drill core trays into a geotechnical log reviewed by a geologist. Segmentation cuts a piece of core where a thin dark line crosses it (the profile layer). - When the geologist corrects the breaks of a box, its runs get a true RQD. Runs of one box share a photo and a calibration, so a box is never in training and test at once.

Done: implemented the four functions in [learning.py](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\learning.py), keeping the docstring, dataclasses, and signatures unchanged, adding only `math` and three small private helpers.

Rules as implemented:

- `mae_of`: mean `|error|` of one candidate over the given runs. Empty run list, a missing run, or a non-finite (`NaN`/`inf`) error used raises `ValueError`.
- `fit`: lowest MAE over the training runs (`None` means every run present); a candidate missing any training run is ineligible. Empty training set, or no eligible candidate, returns the default. MAE ties within 1e-9 break toward the candidate nearest the default (Euclidean distance, also within 1e-9), then the smaller pair.
- `leave_one_box_out`: one fold per box in sorted order; fit on every other box's runs, score default and fitted on the held-out box. Fewer than two boxes returns no folds.
- `learning_curve`: training runs per fold in `(box, run)` sorted order; for `n = 0..max` training size, each fold fits on its first `n` runs and held-out `|error|` is pooled over all folds (`sum/total`); `n = 0` fits on nothing so it equals the default.
